2012_038_071012regmtg.paragraph: Agenda and complete board packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of July 10, 2012, held at 7:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The packet carries minutes of the June 5, 2012 meeting, the June 12, 2012 workshop and the June 19, 2012 regular meeting and budget hearing; five new teacher hires; MHSAA membership for August 1, 2012 through July 31, 2013; four bid awards; and readings of policies B-1204 Quorum, J-2013 Sexting and K-1601 Trademarks. The largest item is the Smart Board award to AVI-SPL for $180,344.00, the last project of the 2004 Bond.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, July 10, 2012, 7:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., except in July and August, and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the June 5, 2012 Board of Education Meeting, the June 12, 2012 Board of Education Workshop, and the June 19, 2012 Board of Education Meeting.

**June 5, 2012 minutes (Athens High School)**
President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti and Schmidt present (Hauff and Underwood absent), Superintendent Fowler, nine administrators, and approximately 140 audience members. An extended recognition block honored Martell Elementary Principal Lois Byrne on her retirement after 7 years, All-State athletes, senior scholar athletes with a 3.5 cumulative grade point average, and dozens of academic teams. Resolution 12-047 issued a two-year probationary contract to Charles Lesser as Principal, Martell Elementary, effective July 1, 2012; 12-048 did the same for Tammy DiPonio at Costello Elementary; 12-049 authorized renewal of the Sodexo Management, Inc. food service contract for 2012/2013 pending Michigan Department of Education approval; 12-050 awarded playground loose fill surfacing material installation to Interlake Landscaping Service, Inc. for $38,825.00; 12-051 set the budget public hearing for June 19, 2012 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road; 12-052 adopted new policy J-2012 Anti-Bullying; 12-053 sent the Board into closed session at 9:28 p.m. under Public Act 267, Section 8(c) for the Superintendent's Evaluation. All votes were 5 yes, 0 no. Adjourned 11:22 p.m.

**June 12, 2012 workshop**
Called to order at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building with all seven members present; agenda items were Visible Thinking and the 2012/2013 Budget Update including the final 2011/2012 appropriation amendment. Adjourned 9:04 p.m.

**June 19, 2012 regular meeting**
The public hearing on the preliminary 2012-2013 budget opened at 7:02 p.m. and closed at 7:15 p.m.; the meeting began at 7:16 p.m. with all seven members present and about 20 audience members. Resolutions 12-054 through 12-069 covered the consent agenda (including the April and May 2012 Treasurer's Report), personnel, renewals with First Student, Enviro-Clean, Coca-Cola and VendTek, two-way radios to Cynergy Wireless Products, Inc. for $20,867.25, fencing to Nationwide Construction Group for $40,153.00, and the budget.

Resolution 12-069 adopted policies B-1302, C-1501, G-1006 Placement of Teachers, G-1401, J-3203, K-1303 and K-1401 on a 6-1 roll call, Schmidt voting no.

**July 10 action items**
Personnel: probationary contracts for Jessica Garrett (.9 FTE School Psychologist, Services Building), Shari Pawlus (1.0 FTE 5th Grade, Barnard), Nicole Schulte (1.0 FTE CI, Wass), Valerie Valentino (.9 FTE English, Troy High) and Autumn Winiarski (1.0 FTE 2nd Grade, Wattles). Curriculum: MHSAA membership for the six secondary schools, effective August 1, 2012 through July 31, 2013.

Agenda and full supporting packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of July 10, 2012, convening at 7:00 PM in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000). Board meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except in July and August, and may be viewed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

MINUTES OF JUNE 5, 2012 (ATHENS HIGH SCHOOL). President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. Present with her were Board members Edmunds, Fleming, Miletti and Schmidt; Hauff and Underwood were recorded absent on every vote. Also present were Superintendent Fowler; administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Goss, Fulcher, Gebbie, Keeling, Machesky, Rajter and Witt; and approximately 140 members of the audience. Recognitions honored Lois Byrne, Principal of Martell Elementary, retiring after 7 years; All-State winter and spring athletes; senior scholar athletes holding a 3.5 cumulative grade point average; 29 eighth graders from Baker, Boulan Park, Larson and Smith Middle Schools with perfect ACT Explore scores; Justin Xu, first in the state with a perfect score in the American Mathematics Competition; the Boulan Park Advanced Orchestra under Kathleen Griffith at the Michigan School Band & Orchestra Association State Festival on May 4, 2012; the Boulan Park Robofest team, the Droids, second nationally at Lawrence Tech; Barnard fourth grader Ben Li in the Michigan Chess Championship; the 2012 Michigan China Quiz Bowl at the Fredrick V. Pankow Center on April 14; twelve Troy High DECA state winners among more than 2,500 competitors; thirteen Troy Creative Minds Destination ImagiNation teams; Michigan Green School Evergreen Status for Hill, Schroeder and Wattles Elementary and Emerald Level for Larson Middle School; the Boulan Park MathCounts state title at Ferris State University; the Michigan Interscholastic Press Association Spartan Award to Athens for its 2010-2011 yearbook Identity; Ananya Mukundan of International Academy East, Grand Award in Physics for "Nano-Tesla Magnetic Field Sensors for an Early Warning System for Earthquakes," and David Bai of Troy High, both advancing to the Intel International Science and Engineering Fair in Pittsburgh; Gold Awards for Troy High Bands at the Heritage Music Festival in San Antonio; Shrutee Rakshit of Wass Elementary, winner of the GovDocKids Constitution Day poster contest and a $50 savings bond; six Athens students who won the Michigan Fed Challenge sponsored by the Detroit Branch of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago and placed second nationally; USA Biology Olympiad semifinalists, 14 of Michigan's 24 honorees coming from Troy High; Farah Huq in the top 50 of the National Biology Competition, in which more than 4,000 students and 300 schools competed and Troy High placed 11th; Dorothy Chen and Sara Ma, top prize in the NASA YouTube Space Lab competition from over 2,000 entries; and Boulan Park sixth grader Kevin Li, first in the Stock Market Game Middle School Division managing a virtual $100,000 over ten weeks.

June 5 public communication came from Steve Dunneback, a Schools of Choice parent of a Costello Elementary student; Judy Gail Armstrong Hall, science teacher at Larson Middle School; and Tony Lucchi, president of the Troy Education Association, all addressing proposed policy G-1006 Placement of Teachers and the Collective Bargaining Agreement expiring June 30, 2013. Resolution 12-047 (Fleming/Edmunds) issued a two-year probationary contract without tenure to Charles Lesser as Principal, Martell Elementary, effective July 1, 2012; 12-048 (Miletti/Schmidt) did the same for Tammy DiPonio at Costello Elementary; 12-049 (Edmunds/Fleming) authorized renewal of the food service contract with Sodexo Management, Inc. for 2012/2013 upon Michigan Department of Education approval; 12-050 (Schmidt/Edmunds) awarded playground loose fill surfacing material installation to Interlake Landscaping Service, Inc. for $38,825.00 from the 2012-2013 General Fund, with Mr. Rajter confirming a biannual resurfacing cycle meeting the state mandate of 12 inches of loose fill under fall areas; 12-051 (Miletti/Fleming) set the budget public hearing for June 19, 2012 at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, Troy 48098, with notice at least six days ahead in 11-point bold faced type. First readings of G-1006 (Edmunds) and J-3203 Children's Internet Protection Act Policy (Fleming) followed; 12-052 (Fleming/Miletti) adopted new policy J-2012 Anti-Bullying; 12-053 (Miletti/Edmunds) moved the Board into closed session at 9:28 p.m. under Public Act 267, Section 8(c), for the Superintendent's Evaluation. The meeting reconvened at 9:45 p.m. and adjourned at 11:22 p.m. Minutes submitted by Todd Miletti, Secretary.

BOARD WORKSHOP, JUNE 12, 2012. Philippart called the workshop to order at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present; administrators Dr. Fowler, Mrs. Keeling, Dr. Machesky, Mr. Rajter, Ms. Papasian, Mr. Cottone and Mr. Whan attended with approximately three audience members. Agenda: Public Communication, Visible Thinking, 2012/2013 Budget Update (Final Appropriation Amendment 2011/2012 and the 2012/2013 Budget), Other; adjourned 9:04 p.m.

SPECIAL BOARD MEETING, JUNE 19, 2012 (SERVICES BUILDING). Philippart opened the public hearing on the preliminary 2012-2013 budget at 7:02 p.m.; Mr. Rajter presented the details and the hearing closed at 7:15 p.m. The meeting began at 7:16 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, Superintendent Fowler, administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Machesky, Miller, Rajter and Witt, and roughly 20 additional audience members. Dr. Fowler gave a final status report on five 2011-2012 Superintendent's Goals: Visibility, Facilities Study, Data Processing Cost Analysis, Strategies for Student Success, and Community Outreach. Tony Lucchi, Judy Gail Armstrong-Hall, teacher Mary Burns and TEA vice president Cindy Shankin spoke against G-1006. Resolution 12-054 (Hauff/Fleming) approved minutes of the May 1 and May 15, 2012 meetings, the May 15, 2012 workshop, and the Treasurer's Report for April and May 2012. 12-055 (Underwood/Edmunds) approved new hires Jessica Bronsteen, Stacie Getty, Jaime Lindstrom, Allison Mason, Brad Sassack and Zaklina Zavich. 12-056 (Fleming/Miletti) issued a two-year probationary administrative contract to William Turner as Assistant Principal, Athens High School, effective July 1, 2012. 12-057 (Edmunds/Underwood) accepted the resignation of Jennifer Gebbie, Assistant Principal, Baker Middle School, effective July 1, 2012. 12-058 (Miletti/Edmunds) extended the Superintendent's contract from July 1, 2012 through June 30, 2015. 12-059 (Hauff/Fleming) extended through June 30, 2014 the contracts of Richard M. Machesky, Assistant Superintendent, Secondary Instruction; Jan Keeling, Elementary Instruction; Mark Rajter, Business Services; and Jasen M. Witt, Human Resources. 12-060 (Schmidt/Underwood) extended administrative contracts through June 30, 2014 for Mark Dziatczak, Lara Dixon, Audra Melton, Timothy Fulcher, Stephanie Acord, Janice Brzezinski, Jerry Cottone, Judith L. Garrett, Mary Haezebrouck, Matt Jansen, David Pass, Jeremy Whan, Robert E. Dowd, Melissa Curth, Brian Canfield, Bettie A. Goss, James Johnson, Remo Roncone, Amy Buchanan, Diane Kocenda, Anthony Morse, Michael Jolly, Kerry Birmingham, Dominick Asaro, Monica Papasian, Anne Mull, Merri Lynn Colligan, Shawna Veit, John Schiesler and Kenneth Miller. 12-061 renewed First Student transportation and 12-062 renewed Enviro-Clean custodial and grounds services, both for 2012/2013 and 2013/2014; 12-063 approved a Coca-Cola beverage vending contract for 7/1/2012-6/30/2015 with up to two additional one-year renewals and 12-064 a VendTek snack vending contract on the same terms; 12-065 awarded two-way radios to Cynergy Wireless Products, Inc. for $20,867.25; and 12-066 awarded fencing to Nationwide Construction Group for $40,153.00, both from the 2012-2013 General Fund. All were 7-0.

BUDGET ACTIONS. Resolution 12-067 (Edmunds/Underwood) amended the fiscal year 2011-12 general appropriations: General Fund $130,776,311, Special Revenue Funds 8,785,651, Debt Service Funds 18,652,488, Capital Projects Fund 4,357,340, Internal Service Fund 116,000. Resolution 12-068 (Miletti/Fleming) approved fiscal year 2012-13 appropriations and millage rates: General Fund $132,398,263, Special Revenue Funds 9,306,329, Debt Service funds 18,480,700, Capital Project Funds/Capital Projects Maintenance Funds 185,000, Internal Service Funds 116,000; 18.0000 mills on Non-Homestead for General Operating, 11.5563 mills on Commercial Personal Property for General Operating, 5.5563 mills on Homestead for General Operating, and 4.9500 mills on All Properties for Debt Retirement. Both passed 7-0. Resolution 12-069 (Underwood/Miletti) adopted policies B-1302 Agendas for Regular Meetings, C-1501 E-mail Retention, G-1006 Placement of Teachers, G-1401 Political Activities, J-3203 Children's Internet Protection Act, K-1303 Commercial Advertising and K-1401 Solicitations on School Property, read respectively by Hauff, Fleming, Miletti, Edmunds, Underwood, Schmidt and Hauff. Mr. Schmidt read a statement opposing G-1006 as having unclear administrative procedures; Mr. Miletti cited Article 24.5 and Article 15 "Transfer" of the Collective Bargaining Agreement; Ms. Philippart noted the underlying law passed in July 2011. Roll call: Fleming yes, Hauff yes, Schmidt no, Underwood yes, Philippart yes, Edmunds yes, Miletti yes; carried 6-1. First readings of J-2013 Sexting (Underwood) and K-1601 (Schmidt) were held for second reading on July 10, 2012. Judy Gail Armstrong-Hall reported the Troy Interfaith Group's Michigan Education Association Humanitarian Award, and Ms. Philippart congratulated the finance department on another ASBO award. Adjourned 9:16 p.m.

JULY 10 PERSONNEL. Probationary contracts recommended for 2012-2013: Jessica Garrett, .9 FTE School Psychologist, Services Building (Eastern Michigan University and Wayne State University; Michigan School Psychologist Certificate September 2009; Livonia Public Schools November 2010-June 2012; resident of Birmingham); Shari Pawlus, 1.0 FTE 5th Grade, Barnard Elementary (Eastern Michigan University and Oakland University; West Bloomfield School District August 2006-June 2012; resident of Waterford); Nicole Schulte, 1.0 FTE CI Teacher, Wass Elementary (Wayne State University and Saginaw Valley State University; Genesee Intermediate School District November 2011-June 2012; resident of Macomb); Valerie Valentino, .9 FTE English, Troy High School (University of Dayton and Boston College; long-term guest teacher in Troy August 2011-June 2012; resident of Bloomfield Hills); and Autumn Winiarski, 1.0 FTE 2nd Grade, Wattles Elementary (Michigan State University; South Lyon Community Schools October 2005-June 2012; resident of Royal Oak).

JULY 10 CURRICULUM AND BUSINESS. The MHSAA resolution enrolls the six secondary schools of the Troy School District, City of Troy, County of Oakland, as members effective August 1, 2012 through July 31, 2013. Bid #9738 for Smart Interactive White Boards, opened June 15, 2012, went to nine bidders with three responses, reviewed by Director of Technology Merri Lynn Colligan and Purchasing Supervisor Sara L. Konieczka (Purchasing Department, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083, 248-823-4052): base bids for 30 units of $117,234.32 from SMARTEd Services, $115,150.00 from AVI-SPL and $117,195.00 from Troxell Communication, with additional-unit totals of 64,436.96, $65,194.00 and $76,294.00. The award to AVI-SPL is $180,344.00 for 46 Smart boards with installation and 18 pro mounts, funded $178,830.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, the remaining balance of the 2004 bond issue and its last project, and $1,514.00 from the 2012-2013 General Fund; 41 boards go to special education classrooms, two to Morse Elementary and two to Wattles Elementary. Bid #9741 for CAD Workstations for Troy High School, opened June 21, 2012 with 13 invitations and five responses (one no bid), drew Howard Technology Solutions at $58,916.00, Civitas-IT at $37,004.00 (base $36,036.00 plus MA1 $968.00), New Tech Solutions at $55,132.00 and Boundary System at $70,906.00; award to Civitas-IT from the 2012-2013 General Fund. Bid #9742 for an Email Archive System, opened June 27, 2012 with three invitations and four responses, drew MBM Computer Systems Solutions at $28,200.93 base with MA1 $298.00, Civitas-IT at $33,259.00, Teoma Systems at $30,205.82 and CIS IT & Engineering at $53,353.81; the recommendation is a Barracuda 650 Email Message Archiver Solution with 3 years of maintenance for $28,200.93, base bid only, supporting the E-Mail Retention policy under which the district retains user e-mail for one year beginning July 1, 2012. Bid #9739 for Kindergarten Classroom Furniture, opened June 20, 2012 with seven invitations and eight responses (one no bid), was split among Dew El Corporations $16,119.70, School Specialty $15,824.48, Global Equipment $4,461.00 and Highsmith $5,541.90 for a total award of $41,947.08 from the 2012-2013 General Fund, outfitting seven additional classrooms for the district-wide all-day Kindergarten program beginning in fall 2012; the bid was developed with Assistant Superintendent of Elementary Education Jan Keeling.

POLICIES. First reading of revised B-1204 Quorum, which sets four members as a quorum, permits a member not physically present to participate by telephone, teleconference or video conference with the presiding chair's permission, and defers to the Open Meetings Act, MCL 15.261 et seq.; adopted January 16, 1979. Second reading of new policy J-2013 Sexting, under Student Rights and Responsibilities J-2000, forbidding sending, sharing, viewing or possessing sexually explicit electronic material at school or school-related activities, authorizing device searches on reasonable suspicion and requiring evidence be turned over to law enforcement; and new policy K-1601 Troy Schools Trademarks, Service Marks, Trade Names and Other Intellectual Property, asserting registration with the Michigan Secretary of State or common-law protection and requiring prior written approval of the Superintendent or designee for any use.
